points.title: Operator reading a customer: which credential and which actor
points.quote: | read a customer | staff, operator preparing a client message | name, phone, e-mail, language |
behaviours: The operator is treated as staff and reads with the staff credential, so the Factory agent holds the staff credential
The operator is a separate caller with its own service token that may read customers, so R0-09's 'needs the staff credential' gets an exception
points.who_notices: The owner, when the Factory's WhatsApp link step cannot read the phone, or when an agent turns out to hold the staff credential

points.title: Operator script publishing artifacts: token or staff credential
points.quote:
The owner service
  must be the service the caller's token names, and the type must belong to
  that service (R0-08, R0-09).
behaviours: onboard_object gets its own service token that names an owner service, and publishes only that service's types
onboard_object uses the staff credential, and staff may publish any type, with the owner service taken from the request
points.who_notices: The operator, when onboard_object's publish is refused, or a reviewer, when staff can publish another service's pointer

points.title: Is the customer's name contact data or project identity
points.unit: R0-06 — The customer is a Registry record (owner, 2026-10-26; closes OQ-01, L03)
points.quote:
how to reach
them — name, phone, e-mail, language.
behaviours: The name is contact data: readable by staff only, wiped on erasure, and the open project card and context carry only customer_ref
The name stays identity: the open project card and context still show the customer's name, and erasure removes only phone, e-mail and language
points.who_notices: PresuPro and Client Portal, which read the 'customer' field of context, and the owner during an erasure request

points.title: Creating or correcting a project with a customer_ref that names no Customer
points.quote: | create a project | staff, consumer service | the project with its identity — supplied by the caller or minted (R0-07) — status `active` | missing name or address refused;
behaviours: An unknown customer_ref is refused, so Cabinet Kernel (which cannot record or read customers) needs a staff-recorded customer before it can create a project
customer_ref is accepted unchecked, and a project may name a Customer that does not exist or does not exist yet
points.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel, when its project creation starts failing; the owner, when the WhatsApp link finds no customer

points.title: Existing projects whose customer_ref predates the Customer record
points.unit: R0-06 — The customer is a Registry record (owner, 2026-10-26; closes OQ-01, L03)
points.quote:
`customer_ref` becomes the Customer's
identity, and a project names its customer by it.
behaviours: Every existing customer_ref value becomes a Customer record with only a name (or none), created at migration
Existing values stay as dangling references until staff record a Customer by hand; reading such a customer answers unknown
points.who_notices: Staff and the operator, the first time they read the customer of an existing project

points.title: No way to find a Customer
behaviours: A 'list customers' (or search by name) action for staff is added, so the frontend can pick a customer when creating a project
Staff must already know the customer_ref; there is no listing, and duplicates of one person are recorded
points.who_notices: Staff using the Registry frontend to attach a customer to a project

points.title: Correcting a customer: overwrite or keep the earlier contact data
points.quote: | correct a customer | staff | the Customer with the new contact data |
behaviours: The new contact data overwrites the old; nothing earlier is kept, so erasure has one place to wipe
Earlier values are kept as history (as Registry otherwise never deletes), and erasure must also wipe every earlier version
points.who_notices: The customer or the owner during an erasure request, when old phone numbers survive

points.title: Erased versus anonymised
points.unit: R0-06 — The customer is a Registry record (owner, 2026-10-26; closes OQ-01, L03)
points.quote: can be erased or anonymised: an explicit exception to R0-03, the only one.
behaviours: The contact fields are removed and the Customer is marked erased, as the 'read a customer' row says
The fields are replaced with placeholder values and the Customer reads as an ordinary record without an erased marker
points.who_notices: The operator preparing a WhatsApp link, who either gets 'erased' or a placeholder phone

points.title: Staff credential: one shared secret or one per person
points.unit: R0-09 — Writes and contact data need a credential (owner, 2026-10-26; closes OQ-04, replaces L15)
behaviours: One staff credential per instance in the protected configuration, shared by everyone on staff
One credential per staff member, so Registry knows which person recorded, corrected or erased a customer
points.who_notices: The owner, when someone leaves and the credential must be revoked, or when asked who erased a customer

points.title: Pointers whose type leaves the configured vocabulary or changes owner
points.unit: R0-08 — The artifact vocabulary is configured, one owner per type (owner, 2026-10-26; closes OQ-03, replaces L08)
points.quote:
The artifact types an instance accepts, and the one owner service of each, are
a list in the instance's configuration, not in the specification: adding a type
needs no spec change.
behaviours: Existing pointers stay listed and readable, and stay withdrawable by the service named on the pointer
Pointers of an unlisted type are hidden or refused on read, and only the type's current owner may withdraw
points.who_notices: A consumer reading history after the configuration changes; a producer whose withdraw is refused

points.title: Create replay of an id whose project is now archived
points.quote: an equal replay returns the existing project, a different one with the same id is refused (R0-07)
behaviours: An equal replay returns the archived project as it is, status archived
The replay is refused because the project is archived (R0-12: archive is final)
points.who_notices: Cabinet Kernel or onboard_object retrying a create, which then either proceeds with an archived project or fails

points.title: Superseded pointer whose artifact the producer deleted
points.quote: a pointer of another service, or already withdrawn or superseded, refused
behaviours: A superseded pointer can never be withdrawn; the history keeps pointing at a deleted artifact without any mark
A producer may withdraw any of its pointers that is not already withdrawn, including superseded ones
points.who_notices: A consumer reading artifact history and following a dead uri

points.title: Who may list rooms after R0-09
points.quote: | list rooms | staff, consumer service | the project's rooms in a declared order |
behaviours: Listing rooms is open to any caller, like 'read a project', which already returns the rooms
Listing rooms needs a staff credential or a service token
points.who_notices: An unauthenticated reader (e.g. the browser) whose room list is refused while the project card shows rooms
